1 · The moment's timeline — LEAD · APPROACH · REST, on both columns

Why the Expected shows j−1 and not something else. The Expected is markup, not a recording: it has exactly two honest states per moment — where the approach starts and where it ends. Showing the end state through the whole approach is what "never moved" looks like; showing the start state through the approach and the end state at rest is the most the Expected can move without inventing frames. The base (the Given as the run found it) is the start of the first moment.
Decided (you, 2026-09-07): the chip is verbatim through the approach. I had proposed that its value line wait for the picture that shows the value; you chose the whole box, every phase. The chip lane in the diagram above should read the same in all three beats.

3 · The one box left — R10's burned card — decided: A

Decided (you, 2026-09-07): option A. The harness paints no card and no pointer into the page any more — only the ring and the dim, on the still and on the film alike (spec/_base.ts renderOverlay). R10's Then is rewritten with the ruling attached; R19's prose that leaned on the card is corrected in place. A re-harvest of every board follows. The options below stay as the record of the choice.

Above, 0.48.5 at 300 ms: the reader's chip ("You typed the task…") and the recording's own card ("R1 · WHEN you type…") on one picture. With the chip now staying through the film (report 3), this overlap remains for as long as the approach plays — the card is pixels in the recording, and no sheet can remove it. It is there because board R10 says: "a callout burned into the recording rings the asserted element and carries the requirement's id chip beside the ONE line that scene is proving". Changing that is a change to R10's text.

A · drop the card from the recording; keep the ring and the dim — recommended

The reader's chip becomes the ONE explanation on every surface, identical in every mode. The whole-requirement video band and the test's evidence video lose their narration card (the ring still says where to look); the run panel's live view loses it too. A re-harvest; R10's Then rewritten by you.

B · keep R10 as written

Two boxes on the Actual while the approach runs, one at rest. Nothing to change; the overlap is accepted.

C · burn the card only while the moment is at rest

The recording keeps a card at each moment's anchor (what the whole-requirement video needs) and none during the gesture (what the per-moment film needs). Still R10's text — it says "the When while the beat is in motion".

6 · After — the demo re-harvested on 0.49.0 (R1, board :4175)

The same R1 row, photographed by a 100 ms probe at each of the three beats in semi-auto. The cycle measured: LEAD 700 ms with the film held on its first frame → the approach 1.0 → 2.27 s of the recording → REST on the still, the Expected switching from the base to moment 1 at that instant → repeat. The chip is the same box, verbatim, in every one of them; there is no burned card in the film any more.

top: LEAD (Expected = the base; Actual = the film's first frame, held) · middle: APPROACH (typing) · bottom: REST (Expected = moment 1's replica; Actual = the photograph)

Two things seen on the way, said rather than hidden. (1) The recording's clock trails the harness by roughly 300 ms: the frame the LEAD holds is about five keystrokes into the typing rather than the empty box. Measured, not corrected — a fixed offset would be a guess (rule 3); a per-recording calibration is a possible follow-up. (2) A CLI harvest against a running board left that board's page naming the recording the same fold had just collected (the watcher rebuilt on the state-guard file BEFORE the fold landed, and nothing rebuilt after): the film was dead until a manual rebuild. The fold now rebuilds board.html itself once its rows have landed.
